//! Database-authoritative release history and explicit dormant pruning.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#4-explicit-pruning-and-audit — no implicit collector or unaudited data loss.
use super::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DormantItem {
    /// Stable cursor; column/index names may coincide.
    pub key: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub action: String,
    pub rows: u64,
    pub bytes: u64,
    pub asset_bytes: u64,
    /// Internal audit distinction: zero standalone cells may still be covered by a dormant row.
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub(crate) definition_only: bool,
    pub sample_ids: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub before_rows:Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub after_rows:Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub restored_rows:Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub before_sample_ids:Option<Vec<String>>,
}

impl DormantItem {
    pub fn unit(&self) -> &'static str {
        match (self.kind.as_str(), self.rows) { ("backfill", 1) => "preimage", ("backfill", _) => "preimages", ("column", 1) => "cell", ("column", _) => "cells", ("index", 1) => "entry", ("index", _) => "entries", (_, 1) => "row", _ => "rows" }
    }
}

impl Store {
    /// Values presently in active rows, independently of table population or other columns.
    pub fn rollback_incompatible_values(&self, current: &Schema, target: &Schema, name: &str, column: &str) -> Result<(u64, Vec<String>), RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.authority_transaction()?;
        let table = &target.tables[name];
        let kind = &table.columns[column];
        if table.engine_field(column) || table.maintained.contains_key(column) { return Ok((0, Vec::new())); }
        let mut count = 0;
        let mut samples = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        let mut statement = tx.conn().prepare("SELECT data FROM r WHERE t=(SELECT num FROM _catalog WHERE name=?1) ORDER BY id")?;
        for data in statement.query_map([name], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0))? {
            let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data?).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
            crate::schema::materialize_optional_fields(&mut row, &current.tables[name]);
            if let Ok(value) = row.field(column)
                && super::narrowed::incompatible_column(&tx, table, name, column, kind, value)? {
                count += 1;
                if samples.len() < 5 {
                    let text = match value { Value::String(s) => format!("'{}'", s.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('\'', "\\'").replace('\n', "\\n").replace('\r', "\\r")), _ => canonical_json(value) };
                    samples.insert(super::adopt_refusals::bounded(&text));
                }
            }
        }
        Ok((count, samples.into_iter().collect()))
    }
}

fn sql_number(n: u64) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
    i64::try_from(n).map_err(|_| {
        RuntimeError::Generation("release counter exceeds SQLite integer range".into())
    })
}

pub(super) fn present(conn: &Connection) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    Ok(conn.query_row(
        "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type='table' AND name='_dormant_tables')",
        [],
        |r| r.get(0),
    )?)
}
pub(crate) fn inventory(
    conn: &Connection,
    after: Option<&str>,
    limit: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<DormantItem>, RuntimeError> {
    if !present(conn)? {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    let narrowed = if super::narrowed::present(conn)? {
        " UNION ALL SELECT c.name,'rows',c.name,NULL FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=n.t GROUP BY n.t "
    } else {""};
    let backfills=super::backfills::inventory_sql(conn)?;
    let query=format!("SELECT path,kind,table_name,column_name FROM (
        SELECT table_name AS path,'table' AS kind,table_name,NULL AS column_name FROM _dormant_tables
        UNION ALL SELECT table_name||'.'||column_name,'column',table_name,column_name FROM _dormant_columns c WHERE table_name NOT IN (SELECT table_name FROM _dormant_tables) OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog t ON t.num=v.t WHERE t.name=c.table_name AND v.column_name=c.column_name)
        UNION ALL SELECT table_name||'.'||index_name,'index',table_name,index_name FROM _dormant_indexes {narrowed} {backfills})
        WHERE (?1 IS NULL OR kind||':'||path>?1) ORDER BY kind||':'||path LIMIT ?2");
    let mut statement=conn.prepare(&query)?;
    let items: Vec<(String, String, String, Option<String>)> = statement
        .query_map(
            params![after, i64::try_from(limit).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)],
            |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?, r.get(2)?, r.get(3)?)),
        )?
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (path, kind, name, column) in items {
        let t: Option<i64> = conn
            .query_row("SELECT num FROM _catalog WHERE name=?1", [&name], |r| {
                r.get(0)
            })
            .optional()?;
        let Some(t) = t else { continue };
        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#11-wave-11-factual-release-narration — dormant row images cover their retained cells; standalone cells have active owners.
        let (mut count,mut bytes):(u64,u64)=match kind.as_str(){
            "backfill"=>conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*),COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id)+octet_length(inputs)+octet_length(before_image)+octet_length(after_image)),0) FROM _backfill_evidence WHERE t=?1 AND definition=?2",params![t,column],|r|Ok((r.get::<_,i64>(0)? as u64,r.get::<_,i64>(1)? as u64)))?,
            "table"=>conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*),COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id)+octet_length(data)),0) FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1",[t],|r|Ok((r.get::<_,i64>(0)? as u64,r.get::<_,i64>(1)? as u64)))?,
            "rows"=>conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*),COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id)+octet_length(data)),0) FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?1",[t],|r|Ok((r.get::<_,i64>(0)? as u64,r.get::<_,i64>(1)? as u64)))?,
            "column"=>conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*),COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id)+octet_length(data)),0) FROM _dormant_values v WHERE t=?1 AND column_name=?2 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE r.t=v.t AND r.id=v.id)",params![t,column],|r|Ok((r.get::<_,i64>(0)? as u64,r.get::<_,i64>(1)? as u64)))?,
            _=>conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*),0 FROM (SELECT id FROM r WHERE t=?1 UNION SELECT id FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1)",[t],|r|Ok((r.get::<_,i64>(0)? as u64,r.get::<_,i64>(1)? as u64)))?,
        };
        if matches!(kind.as_str(), "table" | "rows") {
            let images = if kind == "table" { "_dormant_rows" } else { "_dormant_narrow_rows" };
            bytes += conn.query_row(&format!("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(v.id)+octet_length(v.data)),0) FROM _dormant_values v WHERE v.t=?1 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM {images} d WHERE d.t=v.t AND d.id=v.id)"), [t], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0))? as u64;
        }
        let query = match kind.as_str() {
            "backfill" => "SELECT id FROM _backfill_evidence WHERE t=?1 AND definition=?2 ORDER BY id LIMIT 5",
            "rows" => "SELECT id FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 5",
            "table" => "SELECT id FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 5",
            "column" => {
                "SELECT id FROM _dormant_values v WHERE t=?1 AND column_name=?2 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE r.t=v.t AND r.id=v.id) ORDER BY id LIMIT 5"
            }
            _ => {
                "SELECT id FROM (SELECT id FROM r WHERE t=?1 UNION SELECT id FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1) WHERE ?2 IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 5"
            }
        };
        let mut ids = conn
            .prepare(query)?
            .query_map(params![t, column], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0))?
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|id| super::adopt_refusals::bounded(&id))
            .collect();
        if kind == "index" {
            (count, ids) = index_entries(conn, t, &name, column.as_deref().unwrap())?;
        }
        let asset_bytes = if kind == "index" || kind == "backfill" {
            0
        } else {
            let selector=match kind.as_str(){
                "rows"=>"EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n WHERE n.t=?3 AND n.id=_assets.home_id)",
                "column"=>"EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values v JOIN r ON r.t=v.t AND r.id=v.id WHERE v.t=?3 AND v.id=_assets.home_id AND v.column_name=_assets.home_column)",
                _=>"EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_rows d WHERE d.t=?3 AND d.id=_assets.home_id)",
            };
            conn.query_row(&format!("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(bytes),0) FROM _assets WHERE home_table=?1 AND (?2 IS NULL OR home_column=?2) AND released_at IS NULL AND {selector}"),params![name,if kind=="table" || kind=="rows" {None}else{column.as_deref()},t],|r|r.get::<_,i64>(0).map(|n|n as u64))?
        };
        let definition_only = if kind == "column" {
            !conn.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND column_name=?2)", params![t, column], |r| r.get::<_, bool>(0))?
        } else { count == 0 };
        out.push(DormantItem {
            key: format!("{kind}:{path}"),
            path,
            kind,
            action: "dormant".into(),
            rows: count,
            bytes,
            asset_bytes,
            definition_only,
            sample_ids: ids,
            before_rows:None,after_rows:None,restored_rows:None,before_sample_ids:None,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Retained definitions represent logical entries, rebuilt on restoration.
/// A words index has zero or many entries per image; a row count is not its size.
fn index_entries(conn: &Connection, t: i64, table: &str, index: &str) -> Result<(u64, Vec<String>), RuntimeError> {
    let definition: String = conn.query_row("SELECT definition FROM _dormant_indexes WHERE table_name=?1 AND index_name=?2", params![table, index], |r| r.get(0))?;
    let index: crate::schema::Index = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
    let schema: Option<String> = conn.query_row("SELECT schema FROM _generations WHERE generation=(SELECT CAST(value AS INTEGER) FROM _meta WHERE key='generation')", [], |r| r.get(0)).optional()?;
    let schema: Option<Schema> = schema.map(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))).transpose()?;
    let query = if super::narrowed::present(conn)? {
        "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=?1 UNION ALL SELECT id,data FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1 UNION ALL SELECT id,data FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?1 ORDER BY id"
    } else { "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=?1 UNION ALL SELECT id,data FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1 ORDER BY id" };
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut samples = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    let mut statement = conn.prepare(query)?;
    for image in statement.query_map([t], |r| Ok((r.get::<_, String>(0)?, r.get::<_, String>(1)?)))? {
        let (id, data) = image?;
        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        if let Some(table) = schema.as_ref().and_then(|s| s.table(table)) { crate::schema::materialize_optional_fields(&mut row, table); }
        for cell in conn.prepare("SELECT column_name,data FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2")?.query_map(params![t, id], |r| Ok((r.get::<_, String>(0)?, r.get::<_, String>(1)?)))? {
            let (column, value) = cell?;
            if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
                fields.entry(column).or_insert(serde_json::from_str(&value).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?);
            }
        }
        let entries = crate::rows::index_keys(&index, &row, &id).len() as u64;
        count += entries;
        if entries > 0 && samples.len() < 5 { samples.insert(super::adopt_refusals::bounded(&id)); }
    }
    Ok((count, samples.into_iter().collect()))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#91-per-row-narrowed-value-dormancy — only rows surviving every activation phase count as restored.
pub(crate) fn finalize_restorations(tx:&Tx<'_>) -> Result<(),RuntimeError> {
    if super::live_activation::active(tx)? { return super::live_activation::finalize(tx); }
    let entries=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT key,value FROM _meta WHERE key LIKE 'activation_narrowed_restored_ids:%' OR key LIKE 'activation_column_restored_ids:%' OR key LIKE 'activation_table_restored_ids:%'")?.query_map([],|r|Ok((r.get::<_,String>(0)?,r.get::<_,String>(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
    let mut narrowed=0u64;
    for (key,ids) in entries {
        let (prefix,path)=key.split_once(':').expect("activation restoration key");
        let table=if prefix=="activation_column_restored_ids" {path.split_once('.').expect("column path").0} else {path};
        let count:u64=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?2))",params![tx.num(table)?,ids],|r|r.get::<_,i64>(0).map(|n|n as u64))?;
        tx.set_meta(&format!("{}:{path}",prefix.trim_end_matches("_ids")),&count.to_string())?;
        if prefix=="activation_narrowed_restored_ids" {narrowed+=count;}
    }
    tx.set_meta("activation_narrowed_restored",&narrowed.to_string())?;
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn event(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    operation: &str,
    release: Option<u64>,
    previous: Option<u64>,
    summary: serde_json::Value,
    items: &[DormantItem],
) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    let revision = tx
        .meta("release_revision")?
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(0)
        .checked_add(1)
        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("release revision exhausted".into()))?;
    tx.set_meta("release_revision", &revision.to_string())?;
    let generation = tx
        .meta("generation")?
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1);
    tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _release_events(at,operation,release,previous,generation,revision,summary) VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,?6,?7)",params![crate::now_ms(),operation,release.map(sql_number).transpose()?,previous.map(sql_number).transpose()?,sql_number(generation)?,sql_number(revision)?,summary.to_string()])?;
    let id = tx.conn().last_insert_rowid();
    for item in items {
        tx.conn().execute(
            "INSERT INTO _release_event_items VALUES(?1,?2,?3)",
            params![id, item.key, canonical_json(item)],
        )?;
    }
    Ok(revision)
}

impl Store {
    pub fn dormant_inventory(
        &mut self,
        after: Option<&str>,
        limit: usize,
    ) -> Result<Vec<DormantItem>, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.read_transaction()?;
        let items = inventory(tx.conn(), after, limit)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(items)
    }
    /// One snapshot: current identity, bounded history and storage inventories.
    pub fn release_status(
        &mut self,
        after: u64,
        items_after: Option<&str>,
        event_id: Option<u64>,
    ) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.read_transaction()?;
        let mut events = Vec::new();
        let mut inventory_page = Vec::<serde_json::Value>::new();
        if present(tx.conn())? {
            let mut s=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT id,at,operation,release,previous,generation,revision,summary FROM _release_events WHERE id>?1 ORDER BY id LIMIT 16")?;
            let mut rows = s.query([sql_number(after)?])?;
            while let Some(r) = rows.next()? {
                events.push(serde_json::json!({"id":r.get::<_,i64>(0)?,"at":r.get::<_,i64>(1)?,"operation":r.get::<_,String>(2)?,"release":r.get::<_,Option<i64>>(3)?,"previous":r.get::<_,Option<i64>>(4)?,"generation":r.get::<_,i64>(5)?,"revision":r.get::<_,i64>(6)?,"summary":serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&r.get::<_,String>(7)?).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?}));
            }
            if let Some(event) = event_id {
                let mut s=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT detail FROM _release_event_items WHERE event=?1 AND (?2 IS NULL OR path>?2) ORDER BY path LIMIT 16")?;
                for item in s.query_map(params![sql_number(event)?, items_after], |r| {
                    r.get::<_, String>(0)
                })? {
                    inventory_page.push(
                        serde_json::from_str(&item?)
                            .map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?,
                    );
                }
            } else {
                inventory_page = inventory(tx.conn(), items_after, 16)?
                    .into_iter()
                    .map(|i| serde_json::to_value(i).unwrap())
                    .collect();
            }
        }
        let workers:Vec<(String,String)>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT key,value FROM _meta WHERE key='worker:status' OR key LIKE 'worker:status:%' ORDER BY key LIMIT 16")?.query_map([],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
        let previous_active: Option<u64> = if present(tx.conn())? {tx.conn().query_row("SELECT previous FROM _release_events WHERE release IS NOT NULL AND previous != release AND operation != 'prune' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",[],|r|r.get::<_,Option<i64>>(0)).optional()?.flatten().map(|n|n as u64)} else {None};
        let result = serde_json::json!({"previous_active":previous_active,"release":tx.meta("release")?.and_then(|v|v.parse::<u64>().ok()),"revision":tx.meta("release_revision")?.and_then(|v|v.parse::<u64>().ok()).unwrap_or(0),"generation":tx.meta("generation")?.and_then(|v|v.parse::<u64>().ok()).unwrap_or(1),"native_digest":tx.meta("release_native_digest")?,"events_after":events.last().map(|e|e["id"].clone()),"events":events,"items_after":inventory_page.last().map(|i|i["key"].clone()),"items":inventory_page,"event":event_id,"workers":workers});
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(result)
    }
    pub fn prune_dormant(
        &mut self,
        confirm: bool,
        expected_revision: Option<u64>,
    ) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.transaction()?;
        let held = tx
            .meta("release_revision")?
            .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        if expected_revision.is_some_and(|n| n != held) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation(
                "release revision changed; run releases and retry prune".into(),
            ));
        }
        let items = inventory(tx.conn(), None, usize::MAX)?;
        if !confirm {
            tx.rollback()?;
            return Ok(
                serde_json::json!({"pruned":false,"items":items,"rewrite":"snapback4 prune <dir> --allow-destructive"}),
            );
        }
        if !present(tx.conn())? {
            tx.rollback()?;
            return Ok(serde_json::json!({"pruned":true,"items":[],"revision":held}));
        }
        // Release only dormant homes; active application data is untouched.
        tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _assets SET released_at=COALESCE(released_at,?1) WHERE home_table IN (SELECT table_name FROM _dormant_tables) OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=v.t WHERE c.name=_assets.home_table AND v.column_name=_assets.home_column AND v.id=_assets.home_id)",[crate::now_ms()])?;
        if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {
            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _assets SET released_at=COALESCE(released_at,?1) WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=n.t WHERE c.name=_assets.home_table AND n.id=_assets.home_id)",[crate::now_ms()])?;
            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_values WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n WHERE n.t=_dormant_values.t AND n.id=_dormant_values.id)",[])?;
            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_narrow_rows",[])?;
        }
        let revision = event(
            &tx,
            "prune",
            tx.meta("release")?.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()),
            None,
            serde_json::json!({"dropped_items":items.len(),"bytes":items.iter().map(|i|i.bytes).sum::<u64>(),"asset_bytes":items.iter().map(|i|i.asset_bytes).sum::<u64>()}),
            &items,
        )?;
        let event_id = tx.conn().last_insert_rowid();
        super::backfills::prune(&tx)?;
        tx.conn().execute_batch("DELETE FROM _dormant_values;DELETE FROM _dormant_rows;DELETE FROM _dormant_refs;DELETE FROM _dormant_columns;DELETE FROM _dormant_indexes;DELETE FROM _dormant_tables;")?;
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(serde_json::json!({"pruned":true,"items":items,"revision":revision,"event":event_id}))
    }
}

}

#[test]
fn reentry_restores_shared_snapshots_for_arguments_and_point_reads() {
 let old="table items:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let twice=old.to_owned()+"backfill items twice(n: int):\n  {n:n * 2}\n";
 for later in [false,true] {
  let copied=twice.replace("  n: int","  copied: int\n  lookedUp: int\n  n: int")+"backfill items copy(n: int, id: items):\n  {copied:n, lookedUp:(items[id] ! else NOT_FOUND).n}\n";
  let mut e=engine(old);seed(&mut e,"items",json!({"id":"a","n":3}));
  if later {adopt(&mut e,&twice,2).unwrap();}
  adopt(&mut e,&copied,3).unwrap();let expected=if later {6}else{3};
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","copied"),Value::Int(expected));
  adopt(&mut e,"query empty():\n  return true\n",4).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&copied,3).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","n"),Value::Int(6));assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","copied"),Value::Int(expected));assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","lookedUp"),Value::Int(expected));
 }

fn partial_table_reentry_restores_carried_declarations_in_the_same_cohort() {
 let parents="table parents:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let old=parents.to_owned()+"table children:\n  parent: parents\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let parent_fill="backfill parents twice(n: int):\n  {n:n * 2}\n";
 let next=old.replace("  parent: parents","  copied: int\n  parent: parents")+parent_fill+"backfill children copy(parent: parents):\n  {copied:(parents[parent] ! else NOT_FOUND).n}\n";
 let mut e=engine(&old);seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","n":3}));seed(&mut e,"children",json!({"id":"c","parent":"p"}));adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();
 adopt(&mut e,&(parents.to_owned()+parent_fill),3).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();
 assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"parents","p","n"),Value::Int(6));assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"children","c","copied"),Value::Int(3));
}

fn leaving_the_last_backfill_cannot_remove_an_ended_source_lifetime() {
//! Reads: point lookups, bounded scans with the read rule hoisted where the

//! candidate row is charged to the meter; a query cut by the meter returns
//! what it found and is `capped` (LLP 2000.000 §6).

/// Row-image bytes one execution may step over as expired, unswept rows.
pub(super) const EXPIRED_STEP_GUARD: u64 = 256 << 20;
/// The internal scratch one stepped-over expired row reserves, beside its key.
const EXPIRED_STEP: u64 = 256;

// Only the read evaluator mints key evidence, from evaluated inputs, validated
// cursors, or authorized result positions. Storage images cannot call a raw
// scalar/key pricing API; row fields use AuthorizedRow::scalar_heap instead.
struct DisclosedKey<'a>(&'a Value);
struct DisclosedKeys<'a>(&'a [Value]);
struct DisclosedBounds<'a>(&'a Bounds);
impl DisclosedKey<'_> {
    fn heap(self) -> u64 {
        match self.0 {
            Value::String(s) | Value::Id(s) => word_heap::text(s),
            Value::Bytes(b) => word_heap::allocation(b.len()),
            Value::Array(a) => DisclosedKeys(a).heap(), _ => 0,
        }
    }
    fn copy_heap(self) -> u64 {
        match self.0 {
            Value::String(s) | Value::Id(s) => s.len() as u64,
            Value::Bytes(b) => b.len() as u64,
            Value::Array(a) => {
                word_heap::slots::<Value>(a.len()) + a.iter().map(|v|DisclosedKey(v).copy_heap()).sum::<u64>()
            }
            _ => 0,
        }
    }
}
impl DisclosedKeys<'_> {
    fn heap(self) -> u64 { word_heap::slots::<Value>(self.0.len()) + self.0.iter().map(|v|DisclosedKey(v).heap()).sum::<u64>() }
}
impl DisclosedBounds<'_> {
    fn heap(self) -> u64 {
        let b = self.0;
        [&b.after, &b.at_or_after, &b.before].into_iter().flatten().map(|v|DisclosedKeys(v).heap()).sum::<u64>()
            + [&b.gt, &b.gte, &b.lt, &b.lte].into_iter().flatten().map(|v|DisclosedKey(v).heap()).sum::<u64>()
            + b.word.as_ref().map_or(0, |s| word_heap::text(s))
    }
}

fn key_verdict_heap(index: &crate::schema::Index, prefix: &[Value], viewer: &str, rule: &crate::schema::RuleExpr) -> u64 {
    // The prefix row's collect buffer, map, Arc, viewer and probe term clones.
    let fields = index.components.iter().zip(prefix).filter_map(|(c,v)| c.column().map(|name| (name, v)));
    let row = fields.map(|(name,v)| {
            word_heap::node::<String, Value>() + word_heap::text(name) + DisclosedKey(v).heap()
        }).sum::<u64>();
    word_heap::vec_growth::<(String, Value)>(prefix.len()) + row + word_heap::slots::<usize>(2) + word_heap::text(viewer) + rule_values(rule, prefix, viewer)
}
fn rule_values(rule: &crate::schema::RuleExpr, prefix: &[Value], viewer: &str) -> u64 {
    use crate::schema::{RuleExpr::*, RuleTerm};
    let term = |t: &RuleTerm| match t {
        RuleTerm::Viewer => word_heap::text(viewer), RuleTerm::Literal(v) => DisclosedKey(v).heap(),
        RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } | RuleTerm::Field(_) | RuleTerm::OldField(_) | RuleTerm::NextField(_) => prefix.iter().map(|v|DisclosedKey(v).heap()).sum(),
    };
    match rule {
        Eq(a,b) | Ne(a,b) => term(a) + term(b),
        And(rs) | Or(rs) => rs.iter().map(|r| rule_values(r, prefix, viewer)).sum(), Not(r) => rule_values(r, prefix, viewer),
        Exists { table, key, equalities, .. } | Created { table, key, equalities, .. } => {
            word_heap::text(table)
            + word_heap::vec_growth::<Value>(key.len()) + key.iter().map(term).sum::<u64>()
            + word_heap::vec_growth::<(String, Value)>(equalities.len()) + equalities.iter().map(|(name,v)| word_heap::text(name)+term(v)).sum::<u64>()
        }
        _ => 0,
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.036.001#14 — PAGE admits discovery and target-lane metadata before allocation.
/// Temporary `(table, index)` images built while retaining a rule's complete
/// dependency envelope. Count them without allocating so PAGE lanes can admit
/// the buffer before `rules::probe_sites` clones any names into it.
fn rule_probe_sites_heap(rule: &crate::schema::RuleExpr) -> u64 {
    use crate::schema::{RuleExpr::*, RuleTerm};
    fn term(term: &RuleTerm) -> (usize, u64) {
        term.references().fold((0usize, 0u64), |(count, bytes), (table, _)| {
            (count.saturating_add(1), bytes.saturating_add(word_heap::text(table) + word_heap::text("byId")),
                )
        })
    }
    fn walk(rule: &crate::schema::RuleExpr) -> (usize, u64) {
        let add = |(ac, ab): (usize, u64), (bc, bb): (usize, u64)| {
            (ac.saturating_add(bc), ab.saturating_add(bb))
        };
        match rule {
            Eq(a, b) | Ne(a, b) | Compare(_, a, b) => add(term(a), term(b)),
            Exists { table, index, key, equalities, .. } | Created { table, index, key, equalities, .. } => key.iter().chain(equalities.iter().map(|(_, term)| term)).fold(
                    (1, word_heap::text(table) + word_heap::text(index)),
                    |sum, item| add(sum, term(item)),
                ),
            And(rules) | Or(rules) => rules.iter().fold((0, 0), |sum, rule| add(sum, walk(rule))),
            Not(rule) => walk(rule),
            Allow | Deny | Public { .. } => (0, 0),
        }
    }
    let (count, names) = walk(rule);
    word_heap::vec_growth::<(String, String)>(count).saturating_add(names)
}

    /// How many entries sit under `prefix`, counting at most `limit`.
    pub fn count_prefix(&self, table: &str, index_name: &str, prefix: &[Value], limit: u64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let ti = self.num(&format!("{table}.{index_name}"))?;
        let base = key::encode(prefix);
        let hi = key::upper_bound(&base);
        let count: i64 = self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k >= ?2 AND k < ?3 LIMIT ?4)")?.query_row(params![ti, base, hi, limit as i64], |row| row.get(0))?;
        Ok(count as u64)
    }

    /// Write a row image: a fresh insert when `old` is none, else a replace
    /// that touches only the index entries whose keys changed (a `words`
    /// index has one per token). Returns the number of entries written.
    pub fn put(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value, old: Option<&Value>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.put_indexed(table_name, table, row, old, "INSERT INTO i(ti, k, id) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)")
    }

    /// A replacement loader has already cleared the rows and created its
    /// temporary index heap. It must install those indexes before any read.
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.4 — native replacement sorts complete indexes inside the publication transaction.
    pub fn put_loading_indexes(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.put_indexed(table_name, table, row, None, "INSERT INTO temp._device_index_load(ti, k, id) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)")
    }

    fn put_indexed(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value, old: Option<&Value>, insert_index: &str) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() { return Err(RuntimeError::Store("durable transaction cannot write an ephemeral table".into())); }
        let t = self.num(table_name)?;
        let id = row.field("id")?.as_str()?;
        narrowed::check_write(self,table_name,table,row,old)?;
        backfills::observe_write(self,t,id,table,row,old)?;
        let keys = crate::rows::index_write(table_name, table, row, old, id)?;
        self.changes.borrow_mut().record(table_name, table, old, Some(row));
        let data = canonical_json(row);
        let sql = if old.is_some() { "UPDATE r SET data = ?3 WHERE t = ?1 AND id = ?2" } else { "INSERT INTO r(t, id, data) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)" };
        self.tx.prepare_cached(sql)?.execute(params![t, id, data])?;
        let mut insert = self.tx.prepare_cached(insert_index)?;
        let mut entries = 0;
        for crate::rows::IndexWrite { name, before, after } in keys {
            if before == after { continue; }
            let ti = self.num(&format!("{table_name}.{name}"))?;
            for key in before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)) {
                self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k = ?2")?.execute(params![ti, key])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
            for key in after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)) {
                insert.execute(params![ti, key, id])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
        }
        entries += self.update_cap_counts(table_name, table, old, Some(row))?;
        Ok(entries)
    }

    pub fn delete(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, old: &Value) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() { return Err(RuntimeError::Store("durable transaction cannot write an ephemeral table".into())); }
        let t = self.num(table_name)?;
        self.changes.borrow_mut().record(table_name, table, Some(old), None);
        let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
        dormant::delete(self,t,&id,table_name)?;
        self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id = ?2")?.execute(params![t, id])?;
        let mut entries = 0;
        for (index_name, index) in &table.indexes {
            let ti = self.num(&format!("{table_name}.{index_name}"))?;
            for key in stored_index_keys(table, index, old, &id) {
                self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k = ?2")?.execute(params![ti, key])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
        }
        entries += self.update_cap_counts(table_name, table, Some(old), None)?;
        Ok(entries)
    }

    pub fn next_seq(&self) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM _commits")?.query_row([], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))? as u64)
    }

    /// with the rows it covers).
    pub fn set_meta(&self, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _meta(key, value) VALUES (?1, ?2) ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value", params![key, value])?;
        Ok(())
    }

    }

//! Preflight activation pages before owning their serialized row images.
use super::*;
use crate::{error::MeterKind, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, rows::{adoption, word_heap as heap}};

pub(super) fn walk(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, mut visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    walk_metered(tx, table, adoption::Work::DECODE, None, |id, row, _| visit(id, row))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.24.1 — reserve stored bytes before fetching or decoding; page scratch stays live until consumed.
pub(super) fn walk_metered(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, work: adoption::Work, scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value) -> crate::value::InternalPrice>,
    visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value, &mut Meter) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let checked=|row:&Value|Ok(scratch.map_or_else(crate::value::InternalPrice::zero,|f|f(row)));
    walk_metered_checked(tx,table,work,scratch.map(|_|&checked as &dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<crate::value::InternalPrice,RuntimeError>),visit)
}

/// Row-specific provenance can fail closed before any page callback runs.
pub(super) fn walk_metered_checked(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, work: adoption::Work,
    scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<crate::value::InternalPrice,RuntimeError>>,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value, &mut Meter) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    const PAGE: usize = 256;
    let mut after: Option<String> = None;
    loop {
        // One job meter per page, shared with contribution evaluation. Retain
        // the continuation's allowance across the page; reset only after all
        // its row images and callback scratch have been consumed and dropped.
        let mut meter = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
        meter.at("adopt stored rows");
        meter.heap(after.as_deref().map_or(0, heap::text))?;
        meter.once(crate::meter::HeapSite::SqliteColumns, 2 * tx.page_size)?;
        let page_mark = meter.mark();
        let mut limit = PAGE;
        let mut page = loop {
            limit = work.limit(&meter, limit);
            let sizes = if after.is_some() {
                "SELECT octet_length(id), octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id > ?2 ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            } else {
                "SELECT octet_length(id), octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            };
            let (mut count, mut bytes) = (0, 0u64);
            {
                let mut statement = tx.tx.prepare_cached(sizes)?;
                let mut rows = statement.query(params![table, after, limit as i64])?;
                while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                    let id_bytes = row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as usize;
                    let data_bytes = row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as usize;
                    // Rust-owned text, two native payload copies, allocation
                    // headers and exact Vec slots. Length preflight borrows no
                    // overflow payload (the same SQLite convention as scans).
                    let next = bytes.saturating_add(3 * (heap::allocation(id_bytes) + heap::allocation(data_bytes)) + 64 + heap::slots::<(String, String)>(1));
                    // This first size estimate bounds the fetch; admission below
                    // also checks the actual decoder and contribution allowance.
                    if count > 0 && next > meter.ceilings.heap_bytes / 2 { break; }
                    meter.heap(next - bytes)?;
                    bytes = next;
                    count += 1;
                }
            }
            if count == 0 { return Ok(()); }
            let query = if after.is_some() {
                "SELECT id, data FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id > ?2 ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            } else {
                "SELECT id, data FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            };
            let mut page = Vec::<(String, String)>::with_capacity(count);
            {
                let mut statement = tx.tx.prepare_cached(query)?;
                let mut rows = statement.query(params![table, after, count as i64])?;
                while let Some(row) = rows.next()? { page.push((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?)); }
            }
            if adoption::page_fits_checked(page.iter().map(|(_, data)| data.as_str()), &mut meter, work, scratch)? { break page; }
            limit = (page.len() / 2).max(1);
            drop(page);
            meter.release_heap(page_mark.clone());
        };
        for (id, data) in &page {
            let row_mark = meter.mark();
            meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
            // Decode plus copy-on-write projection, optional materialization
            // and validation scratch. Contribution keys reserve more through
            // this same meter, on top of the still-resident complete page.
            adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::decode_bytes(data))?;
            let row = serde_json::from_str(data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
            visit(id, row, &mut meter)?;
            meter.release_heap(row_mark);
        }
        // Move the last ID into the next page's continuation, without an
        // unpriced clone. Drop every other fetched byte before releasing.
        after = page.pop().map(|row| row.0);
        drop(page);
        meter.release_heap(page_mark);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn fixture(count: usize, payload: usize) -> Store {
        let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        for n in 0..count {
            let id = format!("r{n:04}");
            let data = canonical_json(&crate::value::object([
                ("id", Value::Id(id.clone())), ("payload", Value::String("x".repeat(payload))),
            ]));
            tx.tx.execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) VALUES(1,?1,?2)", params![id, data]).unwrap();
        }
        tx.commit().unwrap();
        store
    }

    #[test]
    fn callback_keeps_the_whole_fetched_page_reserved() {
        let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let mut serialized_bytes = 0;
        for n in 0..20 {
            let id = format!("r{n:04}");
            let data = canonical_json(&crate::value::object([
                ("id", Value::Id(id.clone())), ("payload", Value::String("x".repeat(1024))),
            ]));
            serialized_bytes += (id.len() + data.len()) as u64;
            tx.tx.execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) VALUES(1,?1,?2)", params![id, data]).unwrap();
        }
        let mut calls = 0;
        let mut first_heap = None;
        walk_metered(&tx, 1, adoption::Work::DECODE, None, |_, row, meter| {
            let mut decoder = Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort);
            adoption::charge(&mut decoder, adoption::decode_bytes(&canonical_json(&row)))?;
            let decode = decoder.used.heap_bytes;
            // Independent lower bound: Rust-owned images and both native
            // payload copies coexist with decode. This excludes headers/slots,
            // so it does not just repeat the walker's allocation formula.
            assert!(meter.used.heap_bytes >= 3 * serialized_bytes + decode,
                "Rust and native page copies must coexist with decoder scratch: {:?}", meter.used);
            let expected = first_heap.get_or_insert(meter.used.heap_bytes);
            assert_eq!(meter.used.heap_bytes, *expected, "earlier rows release only their own scratch");
            assert_eq!(meter.used.examined, 20 + calls + 1, "all admission decodes plus callback decodes are charged");
            calls += 1;
            Ok(())
        }).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(calls, 20);
        tx.rollback().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn heap_retries_keep_admission_examinations_at_the_callback_boundary() {
        let mut store = fixture(5, 1280 << 10);
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let work = adoption::Work { examined: 2, steps: 1, index_entries: 1 };
        let scratch = |row: &Value| adoption::contribution_bytes(row, &crate::schema::public_table(Default::default(), Default::default()));
        let mut observed = Vec::new();
        walk_metered(&tx, 1, work, Some(&scratch), |_, row, meter| {
            observed.push(meter.used.examined);
            assert_eq!((meter.used.steps, meter.used.index_entries), (0, 0), "rejected attempts perform no contribution work");
            meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
            meter.step(1)?;
            adoption::charge(meter, scratch(&row))?;
            meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, 1)?;
            assert!(meter.heap_peak <= Ceilings::job().heap_bytes);
            Ok(())
        }).unwrap();
        // Four two-image attempts each decode one row before the heap check
        // asks for a singleton. Its admission and callback decode add two.
        // The last source is already a singleton and needs no rejected attempt.
        assert_eq!(observed, [3, 3, 3, 3, 2]);
        tx.rollback().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_cumulative_budget_fixes_the_page_before_any_callback() {
        for (work, sizes) in [
            (adoption::Work { examined: 64, steps: 63, index_entries: 63 }, vec![252, 4]),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 2, steps: 5040, index_entries: 1 }, vec![198, 58]),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 1, steps: 0, index_entries: 400 }, vec![40, 40, 40, 40, 40, 40, 16]),
        ] {
            let mut store = fixture(256, 0);
            let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
            let (mut page, mut offset, mut calls) = (0, 0u64, 0);
            walk_metered(&tx, 1, work, None, |_, _, meter| {
                assert_eq!(meter.used.examined, sizes[page] + offset * work.examined + 1,
                    "the entire admission pass and every earlier callback remain charged");
                assert_eq!(meter.used.steps, offset * work.steps);
                assert_eq!(meter.used.index_entries, offset * work.index_entries);
                meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, work.examined - 1)?;
                meter.step(work.steps)?;
                meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, work.index_entries)?;
                calls += 1;
                offset += 1;
                if offset == sizes[page] { page += 1; offset = 0; }
                Ok(())
            }).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(calls, 256);
            assert_eq!(page, sizes.len());
            tx.rollback().unwrap();
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_non_fitting_singletons_refuse_before_callbacks() {
        for (work, kind) in [
            (adoption::Work { examined: 16_384, steps: 0, index_entries: 0 }, MeterKind::Examined),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 1, steps: 1_000_001, index_entries: 0 }, MeterKind::Steps),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 1, steps: 0, index_entries: 16_385 }, MeterKind::IndexEntries),
        ] {
            for count in [0, 1] {
                let mut store = fixture(count, 0);
                let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
                let mut calls = 0;
                let result = walk_metered(&tx, 1, work, None, |_, _, _| { calls += 1; Ok(()) });
                assert_eq!(calls, 0, "no callback can start with an impossible page budget");
                if count == 0 { result.unwrap(); }
                else { assert!(matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: got, .. }) if got == kind), "{result:?}"); }
                tx.rollback().unwrap();
            }
        }
    }
}
//! A bounded serialized read-ahead buffer used only inside server activation.
//! Logical callers still fetch and price exactly one row at a time.
// @ref LLP 3000.002#implementation-follow-up — separate bounded raw workspace preserves logical admission.
use super::*;
use crate::{
    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter},
    rows::word_heap as heap,
};
use std::{cell::RefCell, collections::VecDeque};

pub(super) type Buffer = RefCell<Option<Page>>;

pub(super) struct Page {
    table: i64,
    index: i64,
    lo: Vec<u8>,
    hi: Vec<u8>,
    rows: VecDeque<(String, Vec<u8>)>,
    /// Retain the admission for the complete buffer, including consumed slots.
    _meter: Meter,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{engine::InternalLedger, rows::Rows, value::object};

    fn fixture() -> (Store, Schema) {
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), "table entries:\n  n: int\n  text: text <=200000\n  public\n  online only\nquery entries():\n  return entries first 20 by .n\n".into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let schema: Schema =
            serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
        store.install(&schema).unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        for n in 0..96 {
            let row = object([
                ("id", Value::Id(format!("r{n:03}"))),
                ("n", Value::Int(n)),
                (
                    "text",
                    Value::String("x".repeat(if n == 40 { 150_000 } else { 100 })),
                ),
            ]);
            tx.put("entries", &schema.tables["entries"], &row, None)
                .unwrap();
        }
        tx.commit().unwrap();
        (store, schema)
    }

    #[test]
    fn activation_read_ahead_preserves_rows_cursors_and_every_logical_charge() {
        let (mut store, schema) = fixture();
        let index = schema.tables["entries"]
            .indexes
            .iter()
            .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().first().is_some_and(|c| c == "n"))
            .unwrap()
            .0;
        let mut tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
        for n in 0..=96 {
            tx.activation_scan = None;
            let mut slow = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
            let a = InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut slow, |meter, scope| {
                Rows::scan_metered(
                    &tx,
                    "entries",
                    index,
                    &[],
                    &bounds,
                    Dir::Asc,
                    1,
                    scope,
                    meter,
                )
            })
            .unwrap();
            tx.activation_scan = Some(Default::default());
            // Fill/reuse the page by reading the predecessor first, where there is one.
            if n > 0 {
                let before = Bounds {
                    after: Some(vec![Value::Int(n - 2), Value::Id(format!("r{:03}", n - 2))]),
                    ..Default::default()
                };
                let mut ignored = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
                InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut ignored, |meter, scope| {
                    Rows::scan_metered(
                        &tx,
                        "entries",
                        index,
                        &[],
                        &before,
                        Dir::Asc,
                        1,
                        scope,
                        meter,
                    )
                })
                .unwrap();
            }
            let mut fast = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
            let b = InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut fast, |meter, scope| {
                Rows::scan_metered(
                    &tx,
                    "entries",
                    index,
                    &[],
                    &bounds,
                    Dir::Asc,
                    1,
                    scope,
                    meter,
                )
            })
            .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(a, b, "row {n}");
            assert_eq!(slow.used, fast.used, "meter {n}");
            if let Some((_, key)) = a.last() {
                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(key);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn activation_read_ahead_is_invalidated_by_writes_and_raw_access() {
        let (mut store, schema) = fixture();
        let mut tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        tx.activation_scan = Some(Default::default());
        let t = tx.num("entries").unwrap();
        let ti = tx.num("entries.byId").unwrap();
        assert!(
            tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255])
                .unwrap()
                .flatten()
                .is_some()
        );
        let mut row = tx.get("entries", "r001").unwrap().unwrap();
        let old = row.clone();
        if let Value::Row(fields) = &mut row {
            fields.insert("text".into(), Value::String("changed".into()));
        }
        tx.put("entries", &schema.tables["entries"], &row, Some(&old))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        let _ = tx.conn();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        tx.delete("entries", &schema.tables["entries"], &row)
            .unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn raw_projection_and_savepoint_rollback_discard_buffered_images() {
        let (mut store, schema) = fixture();
        let mut tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        tx.activation_scan = Some(Default::default());
        let t = tx.num("entries").unwrap();
        let ti = tx.num("entries.byId").unwrap();
        let old = tx.get("entries", "r001").unwrap().unwrap();
        let mut changed = old.clone();
        if let Value::Row(fields) = &mut changed {
            fields.insert("text".into(), Value::String("temporary".into()));
        }
        tx.savepoint("before_projection").unwrap();
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        // The same getter used by activation's raw projection/staging SQL.
        tx.conn().execute("UPDATE r SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id='r001'",
            params![canonical_json(&changed), t]).unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        // Cache the changed r001 behind r000, then roll the physical write back.
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_some());
        tx.rollback_to("before_projection").unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        let key = crate::rows::index_key(&schema.tables["entries"].indexes["byId"], &old, "r001");
        let (data, _) = tx.activation_head(t, ti, &key, &[255]).unwrap().unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&data).unwrap(), old);
    }
}

impl Tx<'_> {
    pub(super) fn clear_activation_scan(&self) {
        if let Some(buffer) = &self.activation_scan {
            buffer.borrow_mut().take();
        }
    }

    /// None means use the ordinary adapter; Some(None) proves an empty range.
    /// No Value is decoded by read-ahead, so malformed/unvisited payloads do not
    /// change a caller's result or refusal. A too-wide first row uses the old path.
    pub(super) fn activation_head(
        &self,
        t: i64,
        ti: i64,
        lo: &[u8],
        hi: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<Option<Option<(String, Vec<u8>)>>, RuntimeError> {
        let Some(buffer) = &self.activation_scan else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let mut held = buffer.borrow_mut();
        if let Some(page) = held.as_mut() {
            if page.table == t && page.index == ti && page.hi == hi && lo >= page.lo.as_slice() {
                while page
                    .rows
                    .front()
                    .is_some_and(|(_, key)| key.as_slice() < lo)
                {
                    page.rows.pop_front();
                }
                if let Some(row) = page.rows.pop_front() {
                    // Only forward cursors may reuse the unread tail.
                    page.lo = crate::key::upper_bound(&row.1);
                    return Ok(Some(Some(row)));
                }
            }
        }
        held.take();
        const PAGE: usize = 32;
        const BYTES: u64 = 128 * 1024;
        let mut meter = Meter::new(
            Ceilings {
                heap_bytes: BYTES,
                ..Ceilings::job()
            },
            Cut::Abort,
        );
        meter.at("adopt serialized read-ahead");
        let fixed = heap::slots::<(String, Vec<u8>)>(PAGE)
            + heap::allocation(lo.len())
            + heap::allocation(hi.len())
            // upper_bound clones then appends: reserve the old cursor, clone,
            // and the Vec growth replacement together, including capacity.
            + 4 * heap::allocation(2 * crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES + 1)
            + 2 * self.page_size;
        // An unusually large SQLite page can simply disable this optimization.
        if !meter.room(crate::error::MeterKind::HeapBytes, fixed) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        meter.heap(fixed)?;
        let mut count = 0;
        {
            let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT octet_length(r.data), length(i.k) FROM i JOIN r ON r.t = ?1 AND r.id = i.id WHERE i.ti = ?2 AND i.k >= ?3 AND i.k < ?4 ORDER BY i.k LIMIT 32")?;
            let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi])?;
            while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                let bytes = 3
                    * (heap::allocation(row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as usize)
                        + heap::allocation(row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as usize))
                    + 64;
                if !meter.room(crate::error::MeterKind::HeapBytes, bytes) {
                    break;
                }
                meter.heap(bytes)?;
                meter.charge(crate::error::MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
                count += 1;
            }
        }
        if count == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut page = Page {
            table: t,
            index: ti,
            lo: lo.to_vec(),
            hi: hi.to_vec(),
            rows: VecDeque::with_capacity(PAGE),
            _meter: meter,
        };
        {
            let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached(scan_sql(Dir::Asc))?;
            let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi, count])?;
            while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                page.rows.push_back((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?));
            }
        }
        let first = page.rows.pop_front();
        if let Some((_, key)) = &first {
            page.lo = crate::key::upper_bound(key);
        }
        *held = Some(page);
        Ok(Some(first))
    }
}
//! Connection-local activation tuning with a single low-memory retry.
// @ref LLP 3000.002#implementation-follow-up — cache/sorter workspace is configurable, not an RSS ceiling.
use super::*;

pub(super) const ENV: &str = "SNAPBACK4_ADOPTION_CACHE_MIB";
pub(super) const DEFAULT_MIB: u32 = 64;

fn parse(value: &str) -> Result<u32, RuntimeError> {
    value.parse::<u32>().ok().filter(|mib| *mib <= 512).ok_or_else(|| {
        RuntimeError::Input(format!("{ENV} must be an integer from 0 to 512 MiB; 0 retains the caller's cache setting"))
    })
}

pub(super) fn configured_mib() -> Result<u32, RuntimeError> {
    match std::env::var(ENV) {
        Ok(value) => parse(&value),
        Err(std::env::VarError::NotPresent) => Ok(DEFAULT_MIB),
        Err(_) => Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{ENV} must contain an integer from 0 to 512 MiB"))),
    }
}

// Keep headroom for Rust row images, SQLite statements and sorters. This is
// deliberately conservative under an address-space limit, not an RSS promise.
fn bounded_bytes(requested: u64, limit: Option<u64>, mapped: Option<u64>) -> u64 {
    match limit {
        Some(limit) => requested.min(limit / 4).min(limit.saturating_sub(mapped.unwrap_or(0)) / 4),
        None => requested,
    }
}

fn address_space() -> (Option<u64>, Option<u64>) {
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    {
        // procfs avoids introducing unsafe FFI into the core. Missing procfs or
        // an unlimited RLIMIT_AS leaves the explicit caller configuration intact.
        let limit = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/limits").ok().and_then(|s| {
            s.lines().find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("Max address space")?
                .split_whitespace().next()?.parse::<u64>().ok())
        });
        let mapped = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/status").ok().and_then(|s| {
            s.lines().find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("VmSize:")?
                .split_whitespace().next()?.parse::<u64>().ok())
        }).map(|kib| kib.saturating_mul(1024));
        (limit, mapped)
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
    { (None, None) }
}

impl Store {
    pub(super) fn with_activation_cache<T>(
        &mut self,
        mib: u32,
        mut attempt: impl FnMut(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        if mib == 0 { return attempt(self); }
        let schemas = ["main", "temp"];
        let mut original = [0i64; 2];
        let mut bytes = [0u64; 2];
        for (i, schema) in schemas.iter().enumerate() {
            original[i] = self.conn.pragma_query_value(Some(schema), "cache_size", |r| r.get(0))?;
            let page: u64 = self.conn.pragma_query_value(Some(schema), "page_size", |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0))? as u64;
            bytes[i] = if original[i] < 0 { original[i].unsigned_abs().saturating_mul(1024) }
                else { (original[i] as u64).saturating_mul(page) };
        }
        let (limit, mapped) = address_space();
        let requested = u64::from(mib) * 1024 * 1024;
        let budget = bounded_bytes(requested, limit, mapped);
        if budget < requested {
            crate::diagnostic!("snapback4: activation cache target reduced from {mib} MiB to {} KiB for address-space headroom", budget / 1024);
        }
        // A caller that already supplies this much cache keeps both settings.
        if budget <= bytes.iter().sum() { return attempt(self); }
        // Reserve enough temp cache for immediate uniqueness checking during
        // staging. Both caches share the configured target; preserve larger
        // caller settings rather than silently reducing them.
        let target = budget / 2 / 1024;
        let tuned = std::array::from_fn::<_, 2, _>(|i| {
            if target * 1024 > bytes[i] { -(target as i64) } else { original[i] }
        });
        if tuned == original { return attempt(self); }
        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        let result = (|| {
            for (schema, value) in schemas.iter().zip(tuned) {
                self.conn.pragma_update(Some(schema), "cache_size", value)?;
            }
            attempt(self)
        })();
        let nomem = matches!(&result, Err(RuntimeError::Sql(error))
            if error.sqlite_error_code() == Some(rusqlite::ErrorCode::OutOfMemory));
        // The failed transaction has dropped before we can borrow Store again.
        // Never replay an attempt whose transaction remains open; still restore
        // its cache settings on that defensive error path.
        let retry = nomem && self.conn.is_autocommit();
        let released = if retry {
            self.conn.flush_prepared_statement_cache();
            self.conn.release_memory()
        } else { Ok(()) };
        let mut restored = true;
        for (schema, value) in schemas.iter().zip(original) {
            if let Err(error) = self.conn.pragma_update(Some(schema), "cache_size", value) {
                // A committed activation must not become a reported failure
                // because restoring a connection-local hint failed.
                crate::diagnostic!("snapback4: could not restore activation {schema}.cache_size: {error}");
                restored = false;
            }
        }
        if !restored { return result; }
        if retry {
            released?;
            self.conn.release_memory()?;
            // Autocommit alone does not prove the predecessor is still active.
            // A competing publication (or an ambiguous commit failure) must not
            // be replayed under the old in-memory identity.
            if super::activation::identity(&self.conn)? != self.identity { return result; }
            let failed = started.elapsed();
            crate::diagnostic!("snapback4: activation ran out of SQLite memory; rolled back and retrying once with caller main/temp cache_size={original:?} ({ENV}=0 keeps these settings)");
            let result = attempt(self);
            if result.is_ok() && !self.adoption_report.phases.is_empty() {
                self.adoption_report.phases.insert(0, ("memory fallback (rolled back)", failed));
            }
            result
        } else {
            result
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn address_space_headroom_limits_both_caches_together() {
        let mib = 1024 * 1024;
        assert_eq!(bounded_bytes(64 * mib, None, Some(20 * mib)), 64 * mib);
        assert_eq!(bounded_bytes(64 * mib, Some(96 * mib), None), 24 * mib);
        assert_eq!(bounded_bytes(64 * mib, Some(96 * mib), Some(32 * mib)), 16 * mib);
        assert_eq!(bounded_bytes(64 * mib, Some(96 * mib), Some(100 * mib)), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn activation_cache_configuration_has_an_explicit_opt_out_and_range() {
        assert_eq!(parse("0").unwrap(), 0);
        assert_eq!(parse("8").unwrap(), 8);
        assert_eq!(parse("512").unwrap(), 512);
        for value in ["", "-1", "513", "1.5", "fast"] { assert!(parse(value).is_err()); }
    }

    #[test]
    fn activation_cache_retries_only_nomem_once_and_respects_caller_settings() {
        for (budget, original, code, expected_calls) in [
            (64, 7, rusqlite::ffi::SQLITE_NOMEM, 2),
            (64, 7, rusqlite::ffi::SQLITE_FULL, 1),
            (0, 7, rusqlite::ffi::SQLITE_NOMEM, 1),
            (64, -131_072, rusqlite::ffi::SQLITE_NOMEM, 1),
            (8, 7, rusqlite::ffi::SQLITE_NOMEM, 2),
        ] {
            let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
            store.conn().pragma_update(None, "cache_size", original).unwrap();
            store.conn().pragma_update(Some("temp"), "cache_size", 9).unwrap();
            let mut calls = 0;
            let result: Result<(), RuntimeError> = store.with_activation_cache(budget, |store| {
                calls += 1;
                let expected = if budget != 0 && original == 7 && calls == 1 { -i64::from(budget) * 512 } else { original };
                assert_eq!(store.conn().pragma_query_value(None, "cache_size", |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), expected);
                let temp = if budget != 0 && original == 7 && calls == 1 { -i64::from(budget) * 512 } else { 9 };
                assert_eq!(store.conn().pragma_query_value(Some("temp"), "cache_size", |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), temp);
                Err(rusqlite::Error::SqliteFailure(rusqlite::ffi::Error::new(code), None).into())
            });
            assert!(result.is_err());
            assert_eq!(calls, expected_calls);
            assert_eq!(store.conn().pragma_query_value(Some("temp"), "cache_size", |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), 9);
            assert_eq!(store.conn().pragma_query_value(None, "cache_size", |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), original);
        }
    }
}

//! Ownership locks the database's sidecar; stat pins its inode. `serve.lock` is only an address hint.
use std::{fs::{self, File}, io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write}, path::{Path, PathBuf}, time::Duration};
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError, Store};
#[cfg(unix)]
use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;

pub(crate) struct Owner {
    _sidecar: std::sync::Arc<File>,
    identity: (u64, u64),
    path: PathBuf,
    record: Option<File>,
    reclaimed: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) token_authority: Option<crate::serve::token::Authority>,
}

/// The address `doctor` dials for the server that owns this store: the
/// published loopback address itself, or, for a wildcard bind, that family's
/// loopback on the same port. A published non-loopback address is not followed.
pub(crate) fn inspector_address(store: &Path) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    let path = store.canonicalize().ok()?;
    dialable(&address(&path)?)
}

fn dialable(published: &str) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr, SocketAddr};
    let address = published.strip_prefix("http://")?.parse::<SocketAddr>().ok()?;
    let ip = match address.ip() {
        ip if ip.is_loopback() => ip,
        IpAddr::V4(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST),
        IpAddr::V6(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST),
        _ => return None,
    };
    (address.port() != 0).then(|| SocketAddr::new(ip, address.port()))
}

fn resolve(store: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    match store.canonicalize() {
        Ok(path) => Ok(path),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
            let parent = store.parent().filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty()).unwrap_or(Path::new("."));
            snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(parent).map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?;
            Ok(parent.canonicalize().map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?.join(store.file_name().ok_or("store path has no filename")?))
        }
        Err(e) => Err(failure(store, e)),
    }
}

fn failure(path: &Path, reason: impl std::fmt::Display) -> String {
    format!("E_STORE at {}: {reason}; restore a regular store/address file and retry", path.display())
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn same_file(a: &fs::Metadata, b: &fs::Metadata) -> bool { a.dev() == b.dev() && a.ino() == b.ino() }

#[cfg(unix)]
fn regular(path: &Path, create: bool, database: &Path) -> Result<File, String> {
    snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(database, path, create, 128)
        .map_err(|e| failure(path, e))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — sidecar flocks fence backend writers and share device ownership without locking SQLite.
pub(crate) fn command(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, false, Duration::ZERO) }
pub(crate) fn device(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, true, Duration::ZERO) }
// @ref LLP 3000.009#5.3 — a restarting host waits for watchdogs to finish group cleanup.
pub(crate) fn host(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, false, Duration::from_secs(5)) }

#[cfg(unix)]
fn acquire(store: &Path, shared: bool, wait: Duration) -> Result<Owner, String> {
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + wait;
    for _ in 0..16 {
        let path = resolve(store)?;
        snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(path.parent().ok_or("store path has no parent")?)
            .map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        // Stat before opening either auxiliary file; a refused probe creates
        // no database. Only the sidecar lock grants permission to create one.
        let before = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        let sidecar = snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_file(&path)
            .map_err(|e| failure(&snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&path), e))?;
        let mut cleanup = None;
        loop {
            let locked = if shared { sidecar.try_lock_shared() } else { sidecar.try_lock() };
            match locked {
                Ok(()) => break,
                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) if std::time::Instant::now() < deadline && *cleanup.get_or_insert_with(|| stopped_host(&path)) => std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)),
                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => return Err(busy(&path)),
                Err(fs::TryLockError::Error(error)) => return Err(failure(&path, error)),
            }
        }
        if !snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_is_named(&path, &sidecar) { continue; }
        snapback4_core::private_fs::database_file(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        let database = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?
            .ok_or_else(|| failure(&path, "database disappeared during ownership acquisition"))?;
        if before.as_ref().is_some_and(|old| !same_file(old, &database)) { continue; }
        let mut reclaimed = None;
        let record = if shared { None } else {
            let record_path = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
            if let Some(pid)=owner_pid(&path) {
                if unsafe {libc::kill(pid as libc::pid_t,0)} == -1 && std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error()==Some(libc::ESRCH) {
                    reclaimed = Some(format!("reclaimed stale serve.lock: dead PID {pid}; directory {}", path.parent().unwrap().display()));
                }
            }
            let file = regular(&record_path, true, &path)?;
            file.set_len(0).map_err(|e| failure(&record_path, e))?;
            Some(file)
        };
        return Ok(Owner { _sidecar: std::sync::Arc::new(sidecar), identity: (database.dev(), database.ino()), path, record, reclaimed, token_authority: None });
    }
    Err(failure(store, "database path kept changing during ownership acquisition"))
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn acquire(store: &Path, _: bool, _: Duration) -> Result<Owner, String> { Err(failure(store, "database ownership requires Unix")) }

pub(crate) fn stopped_host(path: &Path) -> bool {
    // A CLI owner or a host not yet announced still refuses immediately. A
    // reachable listener does too; only a prior host's cleanup gets a wait.
    // This is a refusal/wait hint, never permission to open the store: the
    // sidecar must still be acquired. Never dial a non-loopback address hint.
    address(path).is_some_and(|published| dialable(&published).is_none_or(|address|
        std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, Duration::from_millis(50)).is_err()))
impl Shared {
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#4-development-doors — current adopted auth policy closes test authority, independently of dev mode.
    pub(crate) fn dev_doors(&self) -> bool {
        if !self.personas { return false; }
        let bound = lock(&self.bound);
        self.unsafe_dev_doors || !(bound.schema.auth.password && !bound.schema.auth.guests)
    }
    // Revalidate under the writer: neither a slow body nor an adoption queue
    // may carry fixture authority into a newly password-only schema.
    pub(crate) fn dev_authority(&self, engine: &Engine) -> Result<(), Refusal> {
        if self.personas && (self.unsafe_dev_doors || !(engine.schema().auth.password && !engine.schema().auth.guests)) { Ok(()) }
        else { Err(dev_doors::closed()) }
    }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 { lock(&self.clock).now().max(self.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire)) }
    pub(crate) fn refresh_time_audience_clock(&self, engine: &Engine, now: i64) {
        if engine.schema().tables.values().any(|table| table.not_before.is_some()) {
            let durable = engine.store().meta("time_audience_clock").ok().flatten()
                .and_then(|value| value.parse::<i64>().ok()).unwrap_or(i64::MIN);
            self.time_audience_clock.fetch_max(now.max(durable), Ordering::AcqRel);
        } else {
            self.time_audience_clock.store(i64::MIN, Ordering::Release);
        }
    }
    fn advance_time_audiences(&self) -> Result<i64, snapback4_core::RuntimeError> {
        let requested = lock(&self.clock).now();
        // Non-timed reader traffic must retain its independent reader lane,
        // including while adoption or a mutation deliberately holds the writer.
        if self.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire) == i64::MIN { return Ok(requested); }
        let mut engine = lock(&self.engine);
        let before = engine.seq()?;
        let now = engine.advance_time_audiences_at(requested)?;
        self.refresh_time_audience_clock(&engine, now);
        if engine.seq()? != before { self.durable_committed(&engine); }
        Ok(now)
    }
    fn next_time_audience(&self) -> Result<Option<i64>, snapback4_core::RuntimeError> {
        if self.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire) == i64::MIN { return Ok(None); }
        lock(&self.engine).next_time_audience_at()
    }
    fn time_audience_delay(&self, at: i64) -> Duration {
        let raw = lock(&self.clock).now();
        let floor = self.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        Duration::from_millis(if at <= floor { 0 } else { at.saturating_sub(raw).max(0) }.try_into().unwrap_or(u64::MAX))
    }
    pub(crate) fn worker_owner(&self) -> Option<Arc<std::fs::File>> { self.owner.as_ref().map(|owner| owner.worker_lock()) }
}
